scenario: [LEXP.3.7.3]: `x.sign_extend(w)` reads the low `w` bits as a two's-complement number: u - 2^w when u >= 2^(w-1), else u, where u = p mod 2^w. Rule `extended` fires where `t.x.sign_extend(t.w)` equals the fact's `want`; every operand is an `Int` slot. `all_ones`: 0xFFF (4095) at 12 bits is -1. `max`: 0x7FF (2047) at 12 bits is 2047, its sign bit clear. `min`: 0x800 (2048) at 12 bits is -2048, its sign bit alone set. `full`: -123456789 at 64 bits is itself, `x.sign_extend(64)` being `x`. A builtin that tested bit `w` instead of bit `w - 1` would get `max` and `min` wrong, and one that shifted by 64 would get `full` wrong. PATH PINNED: FN_SIGN_EXTEND in libds (`builtins.c`, `int_ops.h` `ds_i64_sign_extend`) and Mercury (`ds.eval`).
rules_ds:
schema T scope logical:
    id: String key
    x: Int mutable
    w: Int mutable
    want: Int mutable

rule extended:
    T t where t.x.sign_extend(t.w) == t.want
->
    log info "extended {t.id}"
